accad_14.name: Accad
accad_14.what: One of the first cities of Nimrod's kingdom, in the land of Shinar in southern Mesopotamia.
accad_14.today: Akkad, in central Iraq; exact site unknown.
key: Nimrod's kingdom began with Babel, Erech, Accad, and Calneh in the land of Shinar (Genesis 10).
From there he went into Assyria and built Nineveh and other cities (Genesis 10).

aphek_71.name: Aphek
aphek_71.what: A town in the territory of Asher whose Canaanite inhabitants Asher did not drive out.
aphek_71.today: Likely Tel Afek (Tell Kurdaneh), southeast of Acco in northern Israel.
key: Aphek is listed among the towns of Asher's inheritance, with Ummah and Rehob (Joshua 19).
Asher did not drive out the inhabitants of Aphik, so the Canaanites lived among them (Judges 1).

bileam_248.name: Bileam
bileam_248.what: A Levitical town of western Manasseh given to Kohathite clans, probably the same town as Ibleam.
bileam_248.today: Likely Khirbet Bel'ameh, just south of Jenin.
key: From the half-tribe of Manasseh, Bileam with its pasturelands went to the rest of the Kohathite clans (1 Chronicles 6).
Joshua's parallel list names Gath-rimmon with Taanach from the half-tribe of Manasseh (Joshua 21).

gedor_456.name: Gedor
gedor_456.what: A place in the south where Simeonite clans found rich pasture in King Hezekiah's day.
key: Simeonite clans went to the entrance of Gedor, east of the valley, to seek pasture for their flocks (1 Chronicles 4).
They found rich, good pasture in a land that was very broad, quiet, and peaceful (1 Chronicles 4).
In Hezekiah's days they struck down the Meunim there and settled in their place (1 Chronicles 4).

kain_664.name: Kain
kain_664.what: A town in the hill country of Judah, listed near Zanoah, Gibeah, and Timnah.
kain_664.today: Possibly Khirbet Yaqin, southeast of Hebron.
key: Kain is listed with Gibeah and Timnah among the hill-country towns of Judah (Joshua 15).
It belonged to a group of ten towns with their villages, including Maon, Carmel, and Ziph (Joshua 15).

minni_803.name: Minni
minni_803.what: A kingdom in the mountains north of Assyria, summoned with Ararat and Ashkenaz against Babylon.
minni_803.today: Likely the region south of Lake Urmia, northwestern Iran.
key: Jeremiah summoned the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz to war against Babylon (Jeremiah 51).
They were called up with the kings of the Medes as instruments of the LORD's judgment (Jeremiah 51).

pas-dammim_923.name: Pas-dammim
pas-dammim_923.what: A place in Judah where the Philistines gathered for battle, called Ephes-dammim in the account of Goliath.
pas-dammim_923.today: In the Elah Valley southwest of Bethlehem; exact site unknown.
key: Eleazar son of Dodo was with David at Pas-dammim when the Philistines gathered there for battle (1 Chronicles 11).
They took their stand in a barley field, defended it, and the LORD saved them by a great victory (1 Chronicles 11).
Before Goliath's challenge, the Philistines camped between Socoh and Azekah, in Ephes-dammim (1 Samuel 17).

rephaim_995.name: Rephaim
rephaim_995.what: An early people known for great stature, whose last king, Og, ruled Bashan east of the Jordan.
rephaim_995.today: No single site; their land included Bashan, in northern Jordan and southern Syria.
key: The LORD promised Abraham's offspring the land of the Rephaim among other peoples (Genesis 15).
The Emim and Zamzummim, counted as Rephaim, were displaced by Moab and Ammon (Deuteronomy 2).
Og king of Bashan alone remained of the Rephaim; his iron bed was nine cubits long (Deuteronomy 3).
All Bashan, the region of Argob, was called the land of Rephaim (Deuteronomy 3).

sephar_1048.name: Sephar
sephar_1048.what: A place in the hill country of the east, marking the limit of the lands of Joktan's descendants.
sephar_1048.today: Possibly in southern Arabia; exact site unknown.
key: Joktan's descendants lived from Mesha in the direction of Sephar (Genesis 10).
Sephar is described as the hill country of the east (Genesis 10).

socoh_1105.name: Socoh
socoh_1105.what: A town in Judah's lowland overlooking the Elah Valley, where the Philistines camped before Goliath's challenge.
socoh_1105.today: Likely Khirbet Abbad (Tel Socho), in the Elah Valley, Israel.
key: Socoh is listed with Adullam and Azekah among the towns of Judah's lowland (Joshua 15).
The Philistines gathered at Socoh and camped between Socoh and Azekah before Goliath's challenge (1 Samuel 17).
Rehoboam fortified Soco among his cities for defense in Judah (2 Chronicles 11).
In Ahaz's day the Philistines captured Soco with its villages (2 Chronicles 28).

tiberias_1161.name: Tiberias
tiberias_1161.what: A city on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee, which gave the lake one of its names.
tiberias_1161.today: Tiberias, on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee, Israel.
key: John names the lake as the Sea of Galilee, which is the Sea of Tiberias (John 6).
After Jesus fed the five thousand, boats from Tiberias came near the place where the crowd had eaten (John 6).
